info.desc: "Faith" is the debut solo studio album by English singer George Michael, released on 30 October 1987 by Columbia Records in the United States and on 2 November 1987 by Epic Records in the United Kingdom. Michael wrote and produced all tracks on the album, except for "Look at Your Hands", which he co-wrote with David Austin. Musically, "Faith" is a pop album incorporating elements of R&B, funk, and soul, with lyrics addressing personal and introspective themes that drew attention to Michael's personal life at the time. The album reached number one on both the UK Albums Chart and the .

podcast.body: George Michael's album won Album of the Year in 1989, marking his "first major win." This victory was notable because Grammy voters chose a "pop-upstart" over established Grammy favorites like Bobby McFerrin, Sting, and Steve Winwood, demonstrating their capability to look beyond industry darlings. "When George Michael took album of the year in 1989 with Faith, it was his first major win."

podcast.body: This multi-platinum album generated a half dozen hits for George Michael, spanning genres from funk pop ("I Want Your Sex") and rockabilly (the title track) to soul ballads ("Father Figure," "One More Try"), showcasing his versatility and imperial power. "George Michael's multi platinum album Faith had generated a half dozen hits ranging from the funk pop of I Want Your Sex to the Rockabilly title track to the Soul Ballad's father figure and one more try."
